symptom: after the #2159 caches (ako/mxcli#2160), a quarter of a 600-microflow script was Reader.ListModules and Reader.buildUnitCache: every statement that created a document rescanned the whole Unit table and re-read and re-decoded every module of the project
cause: three things under one symptom. Every write called Reader.InvalidateCache, which marked the list of units stale, so the next read scanned the Unit table again for a write that changed one row. Reader.ListModules read each module's contents and unmarshalled the whole document to take its Name, which the unit index already holds. And Backend.ListModules then read each module's bytes a second time and decoded them with a fresh decoder to fill in the Marketplace details, outside the decode cache. The executor asks for the modules to rebuild its container hierarchy, which it drops after every created document (82 call sites of invalidateHierarchy)
file: modelsdk/mpr/reader_units.go (noteUnitWritten), modelsdk/mpr/writer_core.go (insertUnit, updateUnit), modelsdk/mpr/types.go (ListModules), mdl/backend/modelsdk/backend.go (enrichModule), modelsdk/mprread/generic.go (UnitByIDAs)
insight: Fix the rebuild's cost, not its 82 triggers: with the listing cheap, the executor can go on dropping its hierarchy after every create. For the writer, patch the reader's list for the two writes that dominate (v2 insert and update) and let everything it cannot account for - delete, move, a transaction commit, a stale list, an insert of a row the list already has - fall back to the full invalidation, so the fast path can only be as wrong as its two cases. Then the trap that cost a test run: a Go type registered under two storage names. mprread.UnitByID[*genPr.Module] matches the ONE name TypeNameOf returns (Projects$Module) and a project's modules are Projects$ModuleImpl, so the lookup found nothing, returned no error, and every module silently lost FromAppStore and its version. The test that asserted Atlas_Core's Marketplace details caught it; a test that only counted reads and decodes would have passed. When a count test guards a rewrite of a read, assert a value the read returns as well. Measured on PedApp: Unit table scans per added create statement 1 -> 0; a module listing inside a script run reads 0 files and decodes 0 units where it read two files and decoded one unit per module.
